scenes.heading: Time and time zones
scenes.sub: Why is it morning in Perth and night in London?
scenes.say: When it's lunchtime in Melbourne, it's still morning in Perth and the middle of the night in London. Let's learn twenty-four hour time, elapsed time and time zones.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A Mexican wave travels around a stadium, section by section
scenes.science: Sunrise travels around the Earth: places further east are ahead
scenes.breaks: The wave is smooth, but clocks jump in whole or half hours at borders that follow countries and states.
scenes.say: Think of a Mexican wave at the footy. Each section stands up after the one before it. Sunrise moves around the Earth the same way. Places to the east see the sun first, so their clocks are ahead.

scenes.heading: 24-hour time
scenes.say: In twenty-four hour time, morning times keep their digits, so seven fifteen a m is oh seven fifteen. For p m times, add twelve, so three forty p m is fifteen forty. Midnight is zero hundred, noon is twelve hundred. And remember, an hour has sixty minutes, not a hundred.
scenes.caption: Morning: 7:15 am = 0715. pm: add 12, so 3:40 pm = 1540. Midnight = 0000, noon = 1200. An hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

scenes.heading: Elapsed time: count on
scenes.question: An excursion leaves at 8:45 am and returns at 3:20 pm. How long is it?
scenes.say: An excursion leaves at eight forty-five and returns at three twenty. Count on. Fifteen minutes gets you to nine o'clock. Then six hours to three o'clock. Then twenty more minutes. That's six hours thirty-five minutes.
scenes.caption: 8:45 → 9:00 is 15 min. 9:00 → 3:00 is 6 h. 3:00 → 3:20 is 20 min. Total: 6 h 35 min.

scenes.heading: Count on in jumps
scenes.say: On a time line, the jumps are easy to see: fifteen minutes, then six hours, then twenty minutes. Add the jumps.
scenes.caption: Jumps of 15 min, 6 h and 20 min. Add the jumps: 6 h 35 min.

scenes.heading: Australian time zones
points: Summer: Vic, NSW, ACT, Tas, SA add 1 hour
scenes.say: Time zones are measured from U T C, the world's reference time. Perth is plus eight. Adelaide and Darwin are plus nine and a half. Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane are plus ten. In summer, daylight saving moves Victoria, New South Wales, the A C T, Tasmania and South Australia one hour ahead.
scenes.caption: Times are measured from UTC. Perth +8. Adelaide and Darwin +9:30. Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane +10. In summer, daylight saving adds 1 hour in Vic, NSW, ACT, Tas and SA.

scenes.heading: West is behind, east is ahead
scenes.say: Here are the zones on a line. Perth is furthest west, at plus eight. Then Darwin and Adelaide at plus nine thirty, and Melbourne at plus ten. Moving east, the clocks are ahead.

scenes.heading: Converting between zones
steps: Going east: add. Going west: subtract
scenes.say: To convert, find both offsets and subtract to get the difference. Going east, add it. Going west, subtract it. And if you cross midnight, change the day.

scenes.heading: Melbourne to London
scenes.question: A tournament starts at 11:00 pm Friday in Melbourne (UTC+10). What time is it in London (UTC+0)?
scenes.say: An online tournament starts at eleven p m on Friday in Melbourne. London is plus zero, so the difference is ten hours. London is west, so subtract. Eleven p m minus ten hours is one p m, still Friday.
scenes.caption: Melbourne +10, London +0: 10 hours apart. London is west, so subtract: 11:00 pm − 10 h = 1:00 pm Friday.

points: Count on to find elapsed time
Watch for midnight and daylight saving
scenes.say: Quick recap. Add twelve for p m times. Count on to find elapsed time. Subtract the offsets to get the difference, add going east, subtract going west, and watch out for midnight and daylight saving. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Add 12 for pm times. Count on for elapsed time. Subtract offsets for the difference; east add, west subtract. Watch for midnight and daylight saving. Now try the practice questions!
